extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students of humour, writers and performers interested in wit
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding the characteristics and forms of wit (a form of intelligent humour) and applying or recognising those qualities in writing or performance: brevity, cleverness, repartee, wordplay, and tonal choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as intelligent humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is a form of intelligent humour — the ability to say or write things that are clever and typically funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on cleverness and intelligence in phrasing; wit is characterized by mental sharpness rather than just crude or physical comedy. (Source language: 'Wit is a form of intelligent humour — the ability to say or write things that are clever and typically funny.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity and brevity (one-line/single-phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone witty ... is a person skilled at wit, making spontaneous one-line or single-phrase jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wit often relies on short, immediate remarks rather than long setups; spontaneity and concise form strengthen impact. (Source language: 'making spontaneous one-line or single-phrase jokes.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Quip
rubrics_metrics.description: A quip is an observation or saying that has some wit but perhaps descends into sarcasm, or otherwise is short of a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quips are brief witticisms that may flirt with sarcasm; be aware they can undercut the point if they trade substance for cleverness. (Source language: 'A quip is an observation or saying that has some wit but perhaps descends into sarcasm, or otherwise is short of a point.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Witticism (diminutive effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: A witticism also suggests the diminutive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term implies a small, light or playful piece of wit rather than a weighty insight; suitable for ornament or light amusement. (Source language: 'A witticism also suggests the diminutive.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Repartee (quick comeback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repartee is the wit of the quick answer and capping comment: the snappy comeback and neat retort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing speed and timing: quickness of response and the ability to cap another's remark are central to repartee. (Source language: 'Repartee is the wit of the quick answer and capping comment: the snappy comeback and neat retort.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisecrack (one-line wise joke)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wisecrack is listed as a form of wit (alongside quip and repartee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically a brief, pointed, often sarcastic or ironic remark intended to be funny; functions similarly to quip/repartee in performance or writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingeniousness can trump laugh-out-loud humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Witty remarks may be intentionally cruel (as also in many epigrams), and perhaps more ingenious than funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate wit not solely by laughter produced but by cleverness and intellectual ingenuity; recognize that sharpness or cruelty can be part of the aesthetic. (Source language: 'witty remarks may be intentionally cruel ... and perhaps more ingenious than funny.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordplay combined with conceptual thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit may combine word play with conceptual thinking, as a kind of verbal display requiring attention, without intending to be laugh-out-loud funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use layered linguistic devices and conceptual links; aim for subtle intellectual pleasure rather than overt punchline-driven laughs. (Source language: 'It may combine word play with conceptual thinking, as a kind of verbal display requiring attention, without intending to be laugh-out-loud funny.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit in verse — disguise for poignant feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit in verse can be a thin disguise for more poignant feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In poetic or literary uses, wit can mask deeper emotion or seriousness; consider interplay between cleverness and pathos. (Source language: 'Indeed wit in verse can be a thin disguise for more poignant feelings.')

rubrics_metrics.name: General intellectual attributes (having one's wits)
rubrics_metrics.description: More generally, one's wits are one's intellectual powers of all types; 'to have one's wits about one' is to be alert and capable of quick reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being witty often presupposes alertness and quick reasoning ability; evaluate performers/writers for mental agility as part of wit. (Source language: 'More generally, one's wits are one's intellectual powers ... To have one's wits about one is to be alert and capable of quick reasoning.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Native wit / common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Native wit — meaning the wits with which one is born — is closely synonymous with common sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between learned cleverness and instinctive common-sense resourcefulness; 'native wit' signals an intuitive knack for clever responses. (Source language: 'Native wit — meaning the wits with which one is born — is closely synonymous with common sense.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Social/ethical tone (opportunism and cruelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: To live by one's wits is to be an opportunist, but not always of the scrupulous kind; witty remarks may be intentionally cruel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ethical and social consequences of wit: sharpness or opportunism can alienate audiences; balance cleverness with ethical audience awareness. (Source language: 'To live by one's wits is to be an opportunist ... witty remarks may be intentionally cruel.')
